analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) Asia Equities Update, 2) Decomposing the Rise in US Yields, 3) Hungary's Budget Plan, 4) Cross Asset Trade Ideas and 5) 5 Key Charts 13 Oct 2026
key_insights: Asia saw a rotational semiconductor selloff overnight: KOSPI fell 5-6%, Nikkei 1.5-2% and Taiwan about 2%. Samsung and Hynix dropped 7-10%, with the CXMT news weighing on memory stocks. Privorotsky reads it as an unwind of crowded positions rather than indiscriminate selling.
In Japan, five stocks account for effectively the entire Nikkei decline while TOPIX is trading up slightly. Privorotsky cites this as evidence of a crowded-position unwind.
Privorotsky calls CXMT a legitimate long-term concern for memory economics.

Microsoft's Maia 300 custom chips are moving to TSMC's 2nm process. Privorotsky calls this incrementally negative for merchant GPU suppliers (NVDA) and positive for the custom silicon supply chain and aggregate compute consumption.

Broadcom and Intel reaffirmed strong demand for another 2-3 years, potentially through 2030. Hock Tan sees compute demand exceeding supply, and Privorotsky says Tan's comparison of AI investors to gamblers was taken out of context. Long-term ROI is a legitimate question but not a revelation.

Meta's Muse Wonder and Wonder Full models look competitive at the frontier, potentially adding a serious player alongside OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Prediction markets anticipate another major Google release soon.

Privorotsky's summary is that frontier competition requires more compute, so the news is not bearish for aggregate compute demand even if the economics shift around the supply chain. The legitimate concern is the ability to deliver capacity and power relative to expectations, which is driving further de-rating in the capex vertical.

GS rates research (Marshall) says US Treasury yields rose across the curve. Front-end pricing is hawkish relative to GS economists' Fed baseline, and longer-term forwards are 40-50bp above fair value.

The shift in expected policy path from cuts to hikes, amid higher inflation risks and diminished labor market concerns since the eve of the US-Iran conflict, explains the bulk of the rise in longer-term yields. Better long-run growth expectations and spillovers from abroad also contributed, and 10-15bp of the move is unexplained by the GS framework.
AI investment spending likely contributes through cyclical and long-term growth optimism, but GS finds little evidence that absorbing related debt supply has an outsized or durable impact.

GS estimates bond funds have become underweight duration. With yields elevated versus fundamentals, underweight positioning and diminished technical risks, GS argues for a more bullish stance on US duration.

5y5y UST yields at 5.5-5.6% are close to one standard deviation cheap versus GS's G10 fair value framework. Consensus 1y-ahead short-rate forecasts are up about 125bp YTD, worth about 55bp of longer-term forwards (about 70% of the cumulative move).

MBS and Treasury futures negative convexity amplified the recent selloff, with roughly $60bn in 10y-equivalent MBS hedging flows since early September. Index-level MBS convexity is now about zero and CTD-switch risk is no longer clearly asymmetric to higher yields.
Hungary's Tisza government aims to meet the Maastricht convergence criteria by 2030 and is committed to Euro adoption. The MNB cut its inflation target from 3.0% to 2.5%, the first concrete step.

GS expects Hungary's medium-term budget plan around 15-20 October. GS does not expect a formal Euro entry date (1 Jan 2031 or 2032 are the widely expected candidates), but expects forecasts showing the deficit below 3.0% of GDP by 2029, falling from an estimated 7.5% this year to about 5.0% next year.
GS expects the Hungarian fiscal plan to catalyze Euro-convergence inflows. HUF-EUR 5y/5y swap spreads have roughly halved since the April elections, and GS sees scope for further convergence.

GS structured products pitches Equities Up / EURUSD Down dual-digital trades, citing French fiscal sustainability concerns and widening European government bond spreads that pressure EURUSD while risk appetite stays robust.

GS flags a 0.24% expected increase in September core CPI, a downside surprise bias in DM inflation data in 2026, falling US commercial diesel stocks versus seasonal norms, and a sharp rise in Brazil equity fund inflows.
